title: Regular Hilbert coefficient data for arbitrary defining ideals
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, $M$ a smooth finite-type $k$-scheme, $X\hookrightarrow M$ a closed subscheme of finite type over $k$, and $a\in X$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. No reducedness is assumed. There is an ordered finite list of minimal transverse vertices $\alpha_i$, of positive degrees $d_i=|\alpha_i|$, such that, for every integer $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$, there exists a regular Hilbert coefficient datum at $a$ in the precise sense of [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum]. Thus its regular coefficients, smooth coefficient support, etale ambient chart, supported homogeneous division for every degree prefix, supported generation, invertible block derivative Jacobians and vanishing forbidden derivatives are all on a single neighbourhood; all five conditions hold at every point of its coefficient order locus. Its Taylor ideal is the extension of the actual defining ideal of $X$, including nilpotents. All Taylor-quotient dimensions on the chart are pointwise at most the dimension sequence at its distinguished point. If the Taylor ideal is zero the list is empty, the support is the whole chart and the coefficient ideal is zero. The variables transverse to the support are precisely the essential variables of the vertices. No test propagation or comparison of presentations is asserted.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, route reference; detailed BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1 §§5.2,6.1--6.3,6.5--6.6, read online at https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580; BM2 (1997), Chapter III, especially Theorems 7.14,7.20,9.6. Archival BMT and BM2 WANTED. No Stacks tag states this presentation theorem.

proof.text: Work with the kernel ideal $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_M\to i_*\mathcal O_X)$ of [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. The field spectrum is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $M$ Noetherian. On each affine chart its defining ideal is finitely generated by the definition of a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. It is quasi-coherent by the kernel-ideal statement, hence coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. In all subsequent Taylor extensions use this ideal, not its radical.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is only the resolution-route reference. Preliminary ideal bookkeeping: Stacks Tags 01IN, 01T6, 00FM and 01XZ, in schemes.tex, morphisms.tex, algebra.tex and coherent.tex respectively.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-generic-monotone-diagram] to this closed subscheme at $a$. It gives one etale chart, a monotone initial diagram, ordered minimal vertices and regular ideal generators with those initial exponents and coefficient $1$. Every vertex has positive degree: the residue of every element of the defining ideal at $a\in X$ is zero, so its Taylor ideal contains no unit. Separate the essential variables of the vertices from the complementary variables and group vertices by equal degree. Monotonicity makes the accumulated essential variable sets nested final segments. Fix any finite $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$ only after fixing these vertices.

source.place: BM 1997 Chapter III, (7.1), beginning of Theorem 9.6 proof, pp.261--262 and 278--279; online journal PDF read; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 supplies the route.

proof.text: Induct over the degree blocks. Initially the coefficient scheme is the ambient chart, there are no formal transverse variables or earlier equations, the generators are the regular lifts, and the earlier-test projection is $1$. Retain the fixed first exponents at $a$, membership and generation of the actual Taylor ideal at every point, all earlier derivative equations and their invertible Jacobians, and a regular-coefficient projection onto the common kernel of the earlier forbidden coefficient tests. At block $\ell$, [lem-trf-block-straightening-projection-transport] cuts out the new smooth coefficient scheme by its regular vertex-derivative equations, inverts the new Jacobian, and expands the new transverse variables. It retains the old equations, ideal and first exponents and transports the stored projection coefficientwise. Apply [lem-trf-exact-block-coefficient-projection] to the resulting generators: use its columns $C_\gamma=P^-(T^\beta f_j)$ and matrix $B$, invert $\det B$, and replace only the later generators by $P_\ell f_i$. Later vertices are outside the current prefix diagram, so their first monomials pass its tests. The cited projection therefore preserves their first exponents, the generated ideal and earlier equations, while killing all current forbidden coefficients through degree $Q$. Its finite coefficient-extraction formula again gives the projection required at the next stage. This proves the induction. At the last block the coefficient support $N$ is smooth closed, its transverse variables are exactly the essential variables, all coefficients are regular on the same $N$, and conditions (4),(5) hold at every point of $N$. Each block requires finitely many inversions and there are finitely many blocks; intersect these ambient neighbourhoods.

source.place: BM 1997 Theorem 9.6, (9.7)--(9.8), Remarks 9.9--9.11, Lemma 9.12 and (9.13)--(9.14), pp.279--281; exact simultaneous-projection refinements are the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: Let $S$ be the coefficient order locus. The first exponent of $f_{i,a}$ is $(0,\alpha_i)$, so every coefficient of total degree below $d_i$ vanishes and $a\in S$. Apply [lem-trf-coefficient-locus-uniform-division] to the final regular coefficients. On one neighbourhood, at every $b\in S$ the orders equal $d_i$ and supported homogeneous division holds for every degree prefix and every homogeneous degree. This gives conditions (1),(2). Membership $f_{i,b}\in K_b$ was retained in the block induction. The cited statement uses finitely many stabilization determinants, so this does not require an infinite intersection of open sets.

source.place: BM 1997 completion of Theorem 9.6, p.282, using stabilization Theorem 8.1 and Lemma 7.7.

proof.text: At the distinguished point, [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control] computes the Taylor quotient dimensions as $H_D(t)$ from the initial diagram chosen before the induction. Every straightening is an invertible centered formal substitution, hence carries $(T)^{t+1}$ to $(W,Z)^{t+1}$; all subsequent generator replacements preserve the ideal. Thus the final Taylor ideal $K_a$ still has these dimensions. Apply [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division] with the full-prefix homogeneous division of step 4: equality $H_{K_a}=H_D$ forces zero remainder for every element of $K_a$. This gives supported generation at $a$. Since the generators retain first exponents $(0,\alpha_i)$, a supported sum has its first term in their disjoint assigned orthants (take the least first term of its nonzero summands). Thus the final initial diagram is also $D$.

source.place: BM 1997 Corollary 3.20 and Lemmas 7.3--7.5, pp.239 and 263; Theorem 9.6 retains exponents and the defining ideal.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coefficient-order-hilbert-equality] to the coherent defining ideal, the final smooth coefficient support and its regular equations. Its hypotheses at $a$ are steps 4--5; its derivative-Jacobian and forbidden-derivative hypotheses at every point of $N$ are step 3. It gives $H_{K_b}=H_D$ on $S$ after one ambient shrinking. At each $b\in S$, use [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division] with step 4 and $f_{i,b}\in K_b$. The equality of all quotient dimensions forces zero remainder on $K_b$, hence supported generation there. This is condition (3) simultaneously throughout $S$.

source.place: BM 1997 Theorem 7.14 and completion of Theorem 9.6, pp.265--268 and 282; formal division Lemmas 7.3--7.5.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-extended-hilbert-local-upper-bound] for this same smooth affine chart and closed subscheme. Its final clause supplies the finite-value and finite-module hypotheses for these extended Taylor functions, so its conclusion gives $H_y(t)\le H_a(t)$ for every point $y$ and every $t\ge0$ on one open neighbourhood. Restrict the constructed data to that open. All earlier properties restrict with it. This uses the full relative Taylor variables at nonclosed points, not the dimension of a smaller ordinary completed local ring.

source.place: BM 1997 Remarks 9.1, Lemma 9.3 and completion of Theorem 9.6, pp.275--277 and 282; pointwise finite-witness strengthening is the cited DAG statement; BMT section 6.1 explains the extended convention.

proof.text: If $K_a=0$, [lem-trf-generic-monotone-diagram] supplies the empty regular generating family on a neighbourhood. Its generated defining ideal is zero there. Take $N=U$, no transverse variables, and no coefficients or derivative equations. The coefficient ideal is generated by the empty family, hence zero. Division is just the unique remainder equal to the input polynomial; supported generation says that the zero ideal has only its zero element; all determinant and forbidden-derivative conditions are vacuous. This also covers a zero-dimensional smooth ambient chart. For a nonzero Taylor ideal the preceding construction has positive degrees, and the vertices were fixed before the arbitrary choice of $Q$. In both cases the assembled chart, support, coefficients, Taylor ideals and five properties are precisely a datum of [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum].

source.place: BM 1997 (7.1)--(7.2) and Theorem 9.6, including the empty-diagram case; direct unpacking of the specified datum.

proof_origin.place: Assembly from the existing arbitrary-ideal DAG lemmas following BM 1997 Chapter III, Theorem 9.6 (journal PDF read online; archival local BM2 WANTED). ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the resolution route only.

lean.statement: theorem exists_nonreduced_regularHilbertCoefficientDatum (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k] (X M : Scheme.{u}) (p : M ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (i : X ⟶ M) [IsClosedImmersion i] [Smooth p] [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p] (a : X) : ∃ (m n s : ℕ) (α : Fin s → Fin n →₀ ℕ), orderedVertices α ∧ (∀ l : Fin s, 0 < (α l).degree) ∧ ∀ Q : ℕ, (∀ l : Fin s, (α l).degree - 1 ≤ Q) → ∃ D : RegularHilbertCoefficientDatum p i a m n s α Q, taylorIdeal (RingHom.ker (pullback.snd i D.e).appTop.hom) (D.taylorU D.center) = ⊥ → s = 0 ∧ IsIso D.j ∧ Ideal.span {c | ∃ (l : Fin s) (γ : Fin n →₀ ℕ), γ.degree < (α l).degree ∧ c = D.coeff l γ} = ⊥
